title: Section 125 — Act endangering life or personal safety of others

content.overview: BNS s. 125 — Act endangering life or personal safety of others.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Act endangering life or personal safety of others. BNS restatement of IPC 336. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 336. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 125 is the rule on “Act endangering life or personal safety of others”. The section provides that whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to two thousand five hundred rupees, or with both, but—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 125 exists so that “Act endangering life or personal safety of others” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail
125. Whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to two thousand five hundred rupees, or with both, but—

(a) where hurt is caused, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both;

(b) where grievous hurt is caused, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

Of wrongful restraint and wrongful confinement

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to two thousand five hundred rupees, or with both, but—
2. (a) where hurt is caused, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both;
3. (b) where grievous hurt is caused, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
4. Of wrongful restraint and wrongful confinement

Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:

learningObjectives: Master the tripartite structure of rash and negligent endangerment under BNS s. 125.
Analyze the base offence: rash or negligent act endangering human life or personal safety without causing hurt (up to 3 months or fine up to ₹2,500).
Examine Clause (a): rash or negligent act causing simple hurt (up to 6 months or fine up to ₹5,000).
Examine Clause (b): rash or negligent act causing grievous hurt (up to 3 years or fine up to ₹10,000).
Understand the consolidation of IPC ss. 336, 337, and 338.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 125 consolidates offences of rash or negligent endangerment: whoever does any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others faces imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to ₹2,500, or both; but (a) where hurt is caused, imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both; and (b) where grievous hurt is caused, imprisonment up to three years, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Enforces a graduated scale of penal liability for rash and negligent conduct endangering public safety, escalating penalties proportionately as the outcome progresses from potential risk to simple hurt to grievous hurt.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 125 (consolidating IPC ss. 336, 337, and 338).
Base tier: Doing act rashly or negligently endangering life or safety — imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to ₹2,500, or both (former IPC 336).
Clause (a): Where hurt is caused — imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both (former IPC 337).
Clause (b): Where grievous hurt is caused — imprisonment up to three years, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both (former IPC 338).
Distinction: If death is caused by rash/negligent act, the case ascends to Section 106.
essentialIngredients: The act was done rashly or negligently.
The act endangered human life or the personal safety of others.
For Clause (a): Simple hurt was caused to a person by such act.
For Clause (b): Grievous hurt was caused to a person by such act.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 125 unifies the three progressive provisions of the old IPC into a single integrated section: former IPC 336 (simple endangerment), IPC 337 (causing hurt by endangerment), and IPC 338 (causing grievous hurt by endangerment). The core requirement across all three tiers is a rash or negligent act that creates a direct danger to human life or safety. Criminal rashness requires acting with reckless disregard of potential consequences; criminal negligence requires a gross breach of a duty of care. The section applies to hazardous industrial operations, negligent construction, reckless vehicle navigation, or unsafe handling of machinery. The punishment is calibrated strictly according to the consequence: up to three months for endangerment alone; up to six months if simple hurt ensues; and up to three years if grievous hurt results.
examples: Teaching example (Base tier - Firing celebratory shots): An individual fires live ammunition into the air in a densely populated residential neighborhood during a celebration. No one is hit, but the falling bullets endanger safety. This satisfies the base tier of s. 125 (up to 3 months or ₹2,500 fine).

Teaching example (Clause a - Hurt caused): A builder drops scaffolding poles from a third story onto a pedestrian sidewalk without safety netting, striking a pedestrian and causing bruising. This falls under s. 125(a) (up to 6 months).

Teaching example (Clause b - Grievous hurt caused): A speeding motorist fails to stop at a marked crosswalk, striking a pedestrian and fracturing the pedestrian's hip bone. This falls under s. 125(b) (up to 3 years and fine).
distinctions: Section 125 vs Section 106: Section 125 applies where rash/negligent acts result in endangerment, simple hurt, or grievous hurt; Section 106 applies where death results.
Section 125 vs Section 115/117: Section 125 requires rashness or negligence (no intention to harm); Sections 115 and 117 require intentional or knowing infliction of hurt.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether a crane operator who negligently swung a heavy iron girder over an open public street, which snapped and crushed a pedestrian's foot fracturing several bones, is liable under s. 125(b).
Rule: Doing a rash or negligent act endangering personal safety that causes grievous hurt falls under BNS s. 125(b).
Application: Operating heavy machinery recklessly over an open street is criminally negligent, and bone fractures constitute grievous hurt under s. 116(g).
Conclusion: The operator is guilty under BNS s. 125(b) and punishable with up to three years imprisonment.

keyTakeaways: Consolidates IPC ss. 336, 337, and 338 into a single unified section.
Graduated scale: base endangerment (3 months), causing hurt (6 months), causing grievous hurt (3 years).
Requires criminal rashness or negligence endangering human life or safety.
Gateway provision below Section 106 (which applies when death ensues).
